findings.claim: When you create an account, The Weather Company collects your first name, email address and password.

findings.claim: If you buy an ad-free subscription directly, it asks for your billing address and payment information.

findings.claim: The device information it collects can include your IP address, your device's MAC address, cookies, and features managed on your device such as your calendar.
findings.quote: such as IP address, media access control (MAC) address, and browser cookies and other tracking technology, including features managed on those devices, such as your calendar.

findings.review_reason: Line 269 defines the 'Device information' category the company collects and names IP address, MAC address, cookies and 'features managed on those devices, such as your calendar'; the claim reads it closely.

findings.claim: Besides cookies, the company and its partners may use ETags to recognize when your browser has visited a page before.

findings.surprise_why: ETags are a little-known tracking method that clearing cookies may not remove.
findings.review_reason: Line 130 only defines ETags; the statement that the company and its partners actually use these technologies is in the list's lead-in on line 128.

notes: Covers The Weather Channel, Weather Underground, Storm Radar and SnowCast (US English master text, effective April 30, 2026) with US-state, CCPA, GDPR, LGPD and Korea sections; TWC Shop (Shopify) and the TV network are handled separately. Many key lists (Data Provider enrichment, CCPA sold/shared categories) are one item per line, so some quotes are headings and the context names the listed items. Vendor names and per-product data-rights pages are linked out (Data Vendors page) and not in the text.
